rv.q: The P Word, returning to Bush Theatre, is simply brilliant.
A thoughtful and perceptive production with as much socio-political commentary as heartfelt humanity.
You’ll be thinking about it long after you leave the theatre.
Both actors land hugely funny lines and moments of genuine pathos during the evening, sufficient to render the play's Olivier award more than well deserved.
The play’s ending is a perfect balance of joy and gloom, all marvelously managed in a great production.
The script feels slightly unfocused, prone to overreaching.
The P Word offers a devastating and insightful glimpse into the world of the gay Muslim from two very different perspectives.
It is an emotionally stretching, intellectually engaging evening that leaves you feeling you’ve experienced much more than a play.
A lovely spiky romcom, The P Word is most interesting for the way it exposes two very different cheek-by-jowl versions of Britain.

cn.t: Akhtar's Olivier-winning two-hander about gay Pakistani men earns strong praise for its heartfelt performances and timely themes, though some critics find the script occasionally unfocused and overreaching.
